cards.text: Friend, this message is from the prophet Isaiah, and it's about Zion, another name for Jerusalem. It opens with a voice that flat out REFUSES to quit: "For Zion’s sake I will not keep silent, and for Jerusalem’s sake I will not keep still…" Some people talk when they're nervous. This voice talks until something CHANGES.

cards.question: This voice won't keep still for Jerusalem's sake. How long does it keep going?

answers.text: Until her righteousness shines like a bright light
Until her walls stand tall again
Until the kings send back an answer

cards.text: And when it shines, nations will see her righteousness, and all kings her glory. You can't hide a blazing torch, friend, and I KNOW, because I once tried hiding a smoking batch under a dish towel and the whole kitchen found out anyway.

cards.question: Zion will also be called by a new name. Who gives it to her?

cards.text: Then the picture gets royal. Zion will be a crown of glory, a royal diadem.

cards.question: In this picture, Zion is a crown of glory sitting on a king's head.

cards.text: Not on a head. It's in the hand of the LORD, a royal diadem in the palm of her God. Now about the names she's been called: Forsaken, and her land, Desolate.

cards.question: Zion will go on being called Forsaken.

cards.text: Here's the new name: Hephzibah, and her land gets called Beulah. Friend, I had to practice Hephzibah THREE times before I said it out loud, and I've got a mustache that can tie a bow.

cards.question: Why does Zion get the name Hephzibah and her land the name Beulah?

answers.text: The LORD will take delight in her

cards.text: And her land will be His bride, so now we're at a wedding. Ever see a groom when the doors open and the bride walks in? That man is GONE, friend, grinning like he forgot everybody else is even in the room.

cards.question: As a bridegroom rejoices over his bride, so Zion's God will ___ over her.

cards.text: Now we're up on the walls of Jerusalem. Watchmen have been posted there.

cards.question: The watchmen on Jerusalem's walls get to go quiet at night.

cards.text: Never silent, day or night, like a group chat you leave for TEN minutes and come back to 200 messages. And those who call on the LORD are told to take no rest, and to give Him no rest either.

cards.question: Those who call on the LORD keep at it until what happens?

answers.text: He makes Jerusalem the praise of the earth
The watchmen come down off the walls
The harvest is brought in at last

cards.text: Then the LORD swears an oath, by His right hand and by His mighty arm.

cards.question: The LORD swears something will never happen to Zion again. What is it?

cards.text: No more foreigners drinking the new wine Zion toiled for, either. Back in the Millers' kitchen I'd turn around and half a batch was GONE off the cooling rack, so friend, I feel this one.

cards.question: Those who harvest Zion's grain will eat it and praise the LORD.

cards.text: Then the voice gets LOUD: go out through the gates, build up the highway, clear away the stones, raise a banner for the nations! Friend, it's road construction, except this crew actually SHOWS UP.

cards.question: Who is this highway being prepared for?

cards.text: And the LORD has proclaimed something to the ends of the earth. It's a message for Daughter Zion.

cards.question: What's the big news the LORD proclaims for Daughter Zion?
When Zion's Savior comes, He comes empty-handed.

cards.text: And look at the names now. They will be called the Holy People, the Redeemed of the LORD.

cards.question: And Zion will be called Sought Out, A City Not ___.

cards.text: Sought Out. A City Not Forsaken. Friend, I spent YEARS in the back of a junk drawer, so trust me, I know what a name like that means.

findings.problem: The opening card has 4 sentences: 'Friend, this message is from...', 'It opens with a voice...', 'Some people talk when they're nervous.', 'This voice talks until something CHANGES.'

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: In 62:1 the speaker of 'I will not keep silent' is not identified. It could be the prophet or the LORD. The card calls it 'a voice'. papa-dorin.md says that when he quotes someone speaking as 'I', he says who it is first. The Scripture rules also say to leave open what the text leaves open.
findings.question: When a passage's 'I' speaker is ambiguous (prophet or the LORD), should Papa Dorin name a speaker before quoting, or is an unnamed 'voice' the right way to follow 'leave open what the text leaves open'?

findings.problem: The right answer 'Until her righteousness shines like a bright light' is longer and sounds more like the Bible than the plain wrong answers 'Until her walls stand tall again' and 'Until the kings send back an answer'. That makes it stand out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The card says 'You can't hide a blazing torch', but the baker was never told that her salvation is like a blazing torch. Card 1 stopped the quote before it, and card 2's answer mentions only the bright light. The joke also compares Zion's shining righteousness to hiding a smoking, burnt batch. Verse 2 is about nations seeing her glory, not about something embarrassing failing to stay hidden.

rule.text: A callback only works if its setup came earlier in this lesson or conversation.

findings.problem: Nothing before this true or false card hints that the crown is anywhere but on a head. A thoughtful baker would reason that a crown sits on a head, pick True, and be marked wrong. That makes it a gotcha, not an informed guess.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: The story card has 3 sentences: 'Not on a head.', 'It's in the hand of the LORD...', 'Now about the names she's been called...'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: 'Here's the new name: Hephzibah' identifies the new name the LORD bestows in 62:2 with Hephzibah in 62:4. The text doesn't make that connection, and 62:12 gives still more names.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The joke doesn't hold together. Needing to practice saying 'Hephzibah' has nothing to do with having a mustache that can tie a bow, so the punchline doesn't click.

rule.text: It clicks instantly for any adult, with no explaining.

findings.problem: The question asks why Zion gets the name Hephzibah and her land the name Beulah. The answer 'The LORD will take delight in her' is the reason 62:4 gives for Zion. For the land, the verse says 'your land will be His bride'. The right answer isn't true for both.

rule.text: A card about two groups needs an answer true for both. When a question covers more than one group, like the sea creatures and the birds, the right answer must be true for every group in it.

findings.problem: The story card has 3 sentences: 'And her land will be His bride, so now we're at a wedding.', 'Ever see a groom...?', 'That man is GONE...'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The first half of 62:5, 'as a young man marries a young woman, so your sons will marry you', is never told on any card. Card 11 cites 62:4-5 but only jokes about a groom.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The question gives away its own answer. 'As a bridegroom rejoices over his bride, so Zion's God will ___ over her' already contains 'rejoices', which rules out 'watch' and 'weep' without any thought about meaning.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The joke makes up a moment in the Millers' kitchen: 'I'd turn around and half a batch was GONE off the cooling rack'. papa-dorin.md lets jokes make up small moments around his bakery but says he never adds anything new to his backstory. The Millers' kitchen is backstory, not his bakery. The joke also casts the Millers' family in the role of the enemies and foreigners of 62:8.
findings.question: Can Papa Dorin's jokes make up small moments set in the Millers' kitchen, or only in his Dorinverse bakery?

findings.problem: The second half of 62:9, that those who gather grapes will drink the wine in the LORD's holy courts, is never told. That leaves out where the harvest is enjoyed.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: 'It's road construction, except this crew actually SHOWS UP' is a jab at road crews as a group not showing up for work.

rule.text: Never puts down any person or group: no jokes about age, gender, race, nationality, accents, appearance, intelligence or church denomination.

findings.problem: The story card has 3 sentences: 'Sought Out.', 'A City Not Forsaken.', 'Friend, I spent YEARS...'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
